look_here_first: WHITE TRIDENS: find a narrow, straight, DENSE panicle with spikelets pressed to the axis. The green and pale mature photographs show this architecture. Mature glumes are nearly equal and about 4 mm; lemma faces largely hairless or hairy just at the base. Confirm glume/lemma measurements on an intact ripe spikelet, not whiteness.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Against T. flavus, look for narrowly appressed rather than broad drooping panicle branches; color varies for both. Against T. texanus, the packed almost continuous head versus an often flexuous sparse head is helpful, but dissect a mature spikelet: almost glabrous lemmas (except sometimes extreme base) and nearly equal glumes.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Compare same-scale mature panicles, glumes and dorsal lemma nerve hairs
field_matrix.look_alike: Large perennial with broadly open, many-branched, often nodding panicle (commonly 15–35 cm). Red/purple spikelets in bloom frequently mature dull tan; the two local pictures demonstrate both phases. Compared to Texas tridens, purpletop tends more expansive and larger but panicle lengths overlap; both can show exposed branch bases. Check flattened basal sheaths, short hair-fringe ligule, mature lemma nerve hairs, and possibly sticky panicle branches rather than treating stickiness or color as a mandatory ID.
field_matrix.avoid_false_identification: Color, bare branch segments and height overlap; never assert tiny hairs visible in whole-plant photo.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Compare same-scale mature panicles, glumes and dorsal lemma nerve hairs
field_matrix.look_alike: Perennial grass commonly 20–75 cm with a panicle often about 5–16 cm: slender flexible lateral branches can have long empty lower sections, ending in prominent often pink/rose spikelets with 6–12 florets. Existing mature arching photo and close-up both show these gross characters, but purpletop can have the SAME bare branch feature. For real ID compare the mature glumes about half lemma length and lemma-nerve hairs below midlength; avoid relying on rosy color, panicle droop or bark/soil habitat alone.
field_matrix.avoid_false_identification: Color, bare branch segments and height overlap; never assert tiny hairs visible in whole-plant photo.

field_id_finish_pass.crew_teaching_summary: Often a medium-sized perennial bunchgrass with a tight, lance-shaped upright panicle (Kew ~8–25 cm); appressed branches carry crowded green-to-white/purplish spikelets. Both existing photographs show this distinctly. Compare with purpletop's open head and Texas tridens' flexuous exposed branches. Check nearly equal glumes and restricted lemma-nerve hair distribution under hand lens; current photos are habit only.
field_id_finish_pass.lookalike_comparison: Against T. flavus, look for narrowly appressed rather than broad drooping panicle branches; color varies for both. Against T. texanus, the packed almost continuous head versus an often flexuous sparse head is helpful, but dissect a mature spikelet: almost glabrous lemmas (except sometimes extreme base) and nearly equal glumes.
photo_targets: Full rooted perennial bunch and mature panicle beside centimeter rule
Ripe 4–10 mm spikelet and paired nearly equal ~4 mm glumes at 1-mm scale
Detached dorsal three-veined lemma under 10–40× with a 0.1–1 mm reference, proving whether hairs are absent above the extreme base; show apical teeth and minute mucro.
True collar ligule hair fringe and sheath

measured_diagnostic_key.evidence_scope: Published GrassBase/Kew measurements, not measurements of the two installed overview photos. Preserve provisional taxon/county status.
measured_diagnostic_key.look_here_first: WHITE TRIDENS: find the narrow, upright, crowded flowering head, then at a ripe spikelet verify two nearly equal glumes and a three-veined lemma. Color is unreliable.
measured_diagnostic_key.growth_form: Warm-season tufted perennial with short knotty rhizomes; erect culms 30–90 cm; narrow leaf blades 1–4 mm wide.
measured_diagnostic_key.ligule_collar: Ligule a short fringe of hairs 0.2–0.5 mm at the true blade/sheath junction; document collar at millimeter scale. Auricle condition not established by installed photos.
measured_diagnostic_key.panicle: Contracted lance-shaped panicle 8–25 cm long and 0.6–1.5 cm wide; primary branches appressed, about 2–6 cm long.
measured_diagnostic_key.spikelet: Pedicelled, laterally compressed, 4–10 mm long, usually 4–10 fertile florets with diminished terminal florets; separate florets disarticulate above persistent glumes.
measured_diagnostic_key.glumes: Both membranous, one-keeled and one-veined, about 3–4 mm each, similar in length and shorter than the whole multi-flowered spikelet.
measured_diagnostic_key.lemma_palea: Fertile lemma about 3–4 mm, three-veined, tip toothed or shallowly split with short mucro; palea about 0.9× lemma length. GrassBase reports midvein and margins without cilia; do not infer tiny hairs from overview photos.
measured_diagnostic_key.awns: No long projecting glume awns; lemma tip may be minutely mucronate. Do not mistake mucro for a long awn.
measured_diagnostic_key.lookalikes: Tridens flavus typically has a broader open often drooping panicle; Tridens texanus has flexuous branches and separated terminal spikelet groups. Color and empty lower branch sections alone do not decide either comparison; inspect glumes and lemma nerves.

public_ready_criteria: Keep two existing real source-labelled images, their exact CC BY 4.0/CC0 licenses, attribution and four existing gross-feature arrows.
Same rooted plant: photograph crown and full mature contracted panicle with centimeter ruler, plus same-plant collar and 0.2–0.5 mm ligule with millimeter scale.
Dissect several ripe spikelets at 10–20× with millimeter scale: resolve both glumes, florets, one detached three-veined lemma and palea, with arrows only on visible structures.
Show matched-angle confirmed T. flavus and T. texanus flowering heads; avoid using white color alone as the separator.
Keep FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS and provisional county/taxonomy status until anatomy, public-rights rendering and site QA are independently verified.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Tridens albescens — first recognize the head, then verify spikelet parts
steps: See the first SOURCE-LABELLED PHOTO: use gross branches and spikelets as starting clues, not independent expert taxon confirmation.
Compare second photo to learn variable maturation/color/branch posture.
At 10–20× on a real ripe specimen, remove a spikelet and measure the paired outer GLUMES against a fertile LEMMA.

Under 10–40×, inspect the THREE lemma veins and check that the dorsal lemma is glabrous or has hairs confined to the extreme basal callus. White tridens should NOT be taught as having hairy raised lemma nerves; compare with hairy-veined look-alikes. Neither archived overview photo resolves this.
Check 0.2–0.5 mm hairy ligule/collar and basal sheath on the SAME rooted plant; leave tentative Tridens sp. if reproductive anatomy absent.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Species-level Tridens confidence requires panicle architecture PLUS mature spikelet/glume/lemma anatomy; do not identify from pigmentation alone.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Bare panicle branch bases are not unique to Texas tridens. Source-labelled photos do not establish unreviewed county nativity.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
field_id_short_tiles.details: Follow one culm to the complete mature panicle: white tridens typically has a tight lance-shaped 8–25 cm head only about 0.6–1.5 cm wide, with 2–6 cm branches pressed close to the axis. Panels 0–1 show two color stages. White coloration is NOT required; inspect actual branching and mature spikelets.
field_id_short_tiles.status: VISIBLE GROSS STRUCTURE; ROOTED HABIT STILL MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · TRACE CROWN AND TRUE COLLAR
field_id_short_tiles.details: The published growth form is a warm-season perennial with short knotty rhizomes, 30–90 cm culms and narrow 1–4 mm leaf blades. At the actual inner blade/sheath junction look for a ligule of hairs approximately 0.2–0.5 mm; do not confuse sheath-mouth hairs with the ligule. Neither original image proves the rooted base or measured collar.
field_id_short_tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — ROOTED PLANT AND 0.1–1 MM COLLAR SCALE

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · MEASURE A RIPE SPIKELET
field_id_short_tiles.details: Published GrassBase/Kew measurements give laterally compressed spikelets approximately 4–10 mm long with about 4–10 fertile florets. Photograph one intact ripe spikelet against a 1-mm ruler before separating it. Florets detach above persistent outer glumes; the existing photographs show only gross seedhead architecture.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED MEASUREMENT; ATTACHED CALIBRATED SPIKELET NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · GLUMES, LEMMA AND MUCRO
field_id_short_tiles.details: Two one-keeled, one-veined membranous glumes are approximately 3–4 mm and similar in length. The fertile lemma is approximately 3–4 mm, three-veined and toothed/shallowly split at the tip, with at most a short mucro rather than a long awn. Published hair descriptions should be checked on a detached dorsal lemma; no current image resolves glume boundaries, vein hairs or a tiny mucro.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · COMPARE LOCAL TRIDENS
field_id_short_tiles.details: Panels 2–3 show PURPLETOP (Tridens flavus), typically much more open and often drooping. Panels 4–5 show TEXAS TRIDENS (T. texanus), with fine flexuous branches and separated spikelet groups. These are different-species comparison images, not white tridens. All can vary in color; exposed branch bases and pink spikelets alone are not exclusive. Verify nearly equal glumes and lemma nerve-hair distribution when silhouettes overlap.
field_id_short_tiles.status: LOOK-ALIKE GROSS PHOTOS AVAILABLE; MATCHED MATURE DISSECTIONS MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · PROVE BEFORE PUBLIC-FINISHED
field_id_short_tiles.short: Same-plant collar, glumes and lemma required
field_id_short_tiles.details: Obtain one taxon-verified Central Texas rooted flowering plant and connected panicle; photograph a 0.2–0.5 mm true ligule at 10–20×, intact 4–10 mm spikelets with 1-mm scale, then separate both glumes and a three-veined lemma at 20–40×. Add arrows only to structures visible in the pixels. Keep provisional county/native status and FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS until rights, image integrity, annotation and public site QA pass.
